questions.q: Which setting decides how detailed a Kafka Streams application's metrics are, and what is its default?

options.why: That's a sampling window, not a level.

questions.explain: Streams metrics have three recording levels, `info`, `debug` and `trace`, chosen by `metrics.recording.level` (default `info`).

questions.q: Which TWO statements about Kafka Streams metrics are right?

options.t: A Streams instance also has all the producer and consumer metrics
Streams metrics are only visible on the brokers
options.why: They are client metrics, exposed by the application.

options.t: They are organized by client, thread, task and node or store
Every metric is recorded whatever the recording level
options.why: Many metrics need debug or trace.

options.t: Streams exposes no metrics until the app is stopped
options.why: Metrics are exposed while it runs.

questions.explain: A Streams instance contains all producer and consumer metrics plus its own, in a hierarchy: client, stream thread, task, then processor nodes, state stores and record caches.

questions.q: A Streams application has 4 threads configured, but some have died after uncaught exceptions. Which client metrics show it?

options.why: These describe a running thread's work.

questions.explain: Client-level `alive-stream-threads` is the number of running threads; `failed-stream-threads` counts threads that failed since the client started.

questions.q: Which Streams metric shows how many records a stream thread processes per second?

options.why: That's the consumer's rate, before processing.
That's records per poll, not processed per second.

questions.explain: `process-rate` (stream-thread-metrics) is the average number of processed records per second.

questions.q: A windowed aggregation seems to miss some events. Which task metric shows records being discarded, for example as too late for their window?

options.why: Lag shows unread records, not discarded ones.
Threads didn't fail; records were dropped.

questions.explain: `dropped-records-rate` / `dropped-records-total` count records dropped within a task, recorded at `info` level. Records arriving after a window's grace period are dropped.

questions.q: Which Streams task metric shows how late records arrive, as stream time minus the record's timestamp?

options.why: That measures processing time, not lateness.

questions.explain: `record-lateness-avg` is the average observed lateness of records in ms (stream time minus record timestamp).

questions.q: A Streams operator wants to know whether the application as a whole is running, rebalancing or in error. Which client-level metric gives it?

options.why: That counts threads, not the client's state.
A rate doesn't give the state.

questions.explain: The client-level `state` metric is the state of the Kafka Streams client as a string.

questions.q: A Streams thread seems slow but uses little CPU. Which thread metric shows time spent waiting on Kafka brokers?
questions.explain: `blocked-time-ns-total` is the total time in nanoseconds the thread spent blocked on Kafka brokers.

questions.q: Which Connect metric gives a connector's current state as a value such as running, paused or failed?

options.why: That counts connectors on the worker.
That counts tasks on the worker.

questions.explain: The connector-level `status` metric is one of unassigned, running, paused, stopped, failed or restarting.

questions.q: An alert must fire when any task of connector `jdbc-orders` fails on a worker. Which metric fits?

options.why: That counts connectors, not failed tasks.
A low rate isn't the same as a failure.

questions.explain: `connector-failed-task-count` (connect-worker-metrics, per connector) is the number of failed tasks of the connector on the worker; Connect doesn't restart failed tasks itself.

questions.q: A sink connector is falling behind the topic it reads. Which task metric measures that?
questions.explain: `sink-record-lag-max` is the maximum lag in records that the sink task is behind the consumer's position for any topic partition.

questions.q: A sink connector uses `errors.tolerance=all` with a dead-letter topic. Which TWO task error metrics show bad records being handled?

options.why: That's a consumer metric about log position.

questions.explain: Task error metrics include `total-record-errors`, `total-errors-logged` and `deadletterqueue-produce-requests` (attempted writes to the dead-letter queue).

questions.q: Which task metric shows how long a sink task takes to write a batch to the external system?

options.why: That's a source task polling its system.

questions.explain: `put-batch-avg-time-ms` is the average time a sink task takes to put a batch of records; source tasks have `poll-batch-avg-time-ms`.

questions.q: Besides its own metrics, which metrics does a Connect worker process expose?

options.t: Only broker metrics for the cluster it connects to
options.why: Workers expose client metrics, not broker ones.

options.t: None; Connect metrics replace the client ones
All the producer and consumer metrics

questions.explain: A Connect worker process contains all the producer and consumer metrics, plus Connect's worker, connector and task metrics.

questions.q: Producers using `acks=all` see slower writes. Which broker metric should be 0 normally and points at replicas falling behind?

options.why: That shows which broker is the active controller.

questions.explain: `UnderReplicatedPartitions` is normally 0. Above 0, some partitions have replicas that have fallen out of sync, so fewer copies stand behind each acknowledged write.

questions.q: Producers with `acks=all` start failing with NotEnoughReplicasException. Which broker metric confirms the cause?

options.why: Expansion means replicas are rejoining, not missing.
That's unclean elections, a different problem.

questions.explain: `UnderMinIsrPartitionCount` (normally 0) counts partitions whose ISR is below `min.insync.replicas`, where acks=all writes are refused.

questions.q: What is the normal value of `ActiveControllerCount` across a healthy cluster?

options.t: Equal to the number of controllers in the quorum
options.why: Only one controller is active at a time.

options.t: Exactly one node reports 1; the rest 0

questions.explain: Exactly one node should have `ActiveControllerCount` at 1: there is one active controller.

questions.q: Client requests get slower and slower. Which TWO broker metrics show whether the brokers' request threads are overloaded?
questions.explain: `RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent` and `NetworkProcessorAvgIdlePercent` are between 0 and 1, ideally above 0.3; low values mean busy request handling.

questions.q: A broker's `TotalTimeMs` for produce requests is high. How can the team find which stage is slow?

options.t: Compare request-latency-avg across all the producer clients instead
options.why: That shows the total from the client side, not the stages.

options.t: It's split into queue, local, remote and response-send times
Restart the broker to reset the metric
Read the broker's GC log only
options.why: GC is one possible cause; the metric breakdown shows the stage.

questions.explain: `TotalTimeMs` per request type is broken down into queue, local, remote and response-send time, showing where the time goes.

questions.q: Which client-side measures does the Kafka monitoring documentation recommend watching?

options.t: Message and byte rates, request rate/size/time, and consumer max lag and min fetch rate
Only the number of open files

options.why: Topic count isn't a client health signal.

questions.explain: The docs recommend, on clients, message/byte rate (global and per topic), request rate/size/time, and on consumers max lag and min fetch rate.

questions.q: Commits seem to slow a consumer's loop. Which metric measures them?

options.why: That's the gap between polls, which commits are only part of.

questions.explain: `commit-latency-avg` (consumer-coordinator-metrics) is the average time taken for a commit request.
